newsitem.title: GERMANY: German states seal merger of public broadcasters.
newsitem.headline: German states seal merger of public broadcasters.

text.p: The German state governments of Baden-Wuerttemberg and Rheinland-Palatinate approved the merger of two regional public broadcasters, state authorities said on Tuesday.

The Rhineland-Palatinate government said the premiers of the southwestern states, Erwin Teufel and Kurt Beck, planned to initial the agreement for the new television and radio broadcaster, Suedwestrundfunk, in Mannheim on Tuesday.
"Both permiers are very satisfied with the outcome of their negotiations," a spokesman for the Rhineland-Palatinate government said.
"We have succeeded in creating a broadcasting system that will reach throughout the southwest, from Lake Constance to Bonn," he said.

The premiers negotiated the merger of Suedwestfunk and Sueddeutsche Rundfunk for several months before agreeing to final terms for the broadcaster, which will create the second largest station within the ARD public broadcasting network.
The head of Suedwestrundfunk will be based in Stuttgart, with regional management offices in each of the two states, political sources said.
